Applicability has no clear difference by its reported test, despite the broader significance claim in the surrounding means paragraph.

confirmed: Random assignment is explicit: participants were assigned to the experimental or control group and then worked in teams on healthcare and automotive innovation proposals. The assisted group used a GPT-4 Turbo tool; the control received no AI support (PDF p. 4, printed p. 2, section 1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 10, section 4). This study belongs in the two-screener pipeline.

The lab_rct classification is consistent with the codebook's supervised-session definition: students worked in separate rooms and at separate stations. The authors call it a framed field experiment; context_class = none is appropriate for this randomized assistance study (PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 11–12, section 4.1).

The paper reports 70 students, 24 teams and 48 unique ideas. The form distinguishes people from teams and outputs, and explains that n_analyzed = 70 is the reported study sample rather than a separately enumerated post-exclusion count. Separate randomized/analyzed totals, arm-level participant counts and an attrition breakdown are not provided, so those unreported counts cannot be confirmed (PDF p. 14, printed p. 12, section 4.1; full-document review).

The reported main sample exceeds the 50-person threshold; the 24 teams and 48 ideas are not grounds for classifying it as a fewer-than-50-person experiment. The description of three-person teams is not reconciled with the stated 70 students in 24 teams, as the form already notes (PDF p. 12, printed p. 10, section 4; PDF p. 14, printed p. 12, section 4.1).

The separate tool-development work used fifteen participants across three usability studies; this is not the main randomized ideation sample and no creativity contrast from those usability studies is reported (PDF p. 13, printed p. 11, section 4.1).

The GPT-4 Turbo tool generated four specialist AI personas and used temperature zero; the task maximum was 45 minutes, with earlier submission allowed (PDF p. 4, printed p. 2, section 1; PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 11–12, section 4.1).

The S1-O1 reported string and one_line_finding match exactly: aggregate experimental mean 4.583 versus control 3.546; Table 2 t = -4.450938, p = 0.000056, asterisked in the table (PDF p. 16, printed p. 14, section 5; PDF p. 18, printed p. 16, Table 2).

The S1-O2 reported string matches exactly: originality experimental mean 4.819 versus control 3.889; Table 2 t = -2.840212, p = 0.00678, asterisked in the table (PDF p. 16, printed p. 14, section 5; PDF p. 18, printed p. 16, Table 2).

The outcome analysis unit is output: the methods describe mean quality scores per idea and combine the task datasets. The paper does not describe a team-cluster adjustment for the reported independent t-tests (PDF p. 15, printed p. 13, sections 4.2–5; PDF p. 18, printed p. 16, Table 2 and accompanying text).

The diversity claim concerns novelty, feasibility and relevance; no separate between-team similarity or diversity statistic is reported. The form correctly qualifies this claim (PDF p. 14, printed p. 12, section 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 19, section 5).

The source is the 41-page local preprint titled The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Ideation and the performance of Innovation Teams (Preprint), with authors Gindert Michael and Müller Marvin Lutz and title-page date 24 August 2024. No arXiv revision identifier is printed for this document; the source.version description is supported (PDF p. 1; PDF page count and full-document review).

Appendix 1 occupies PDF pp. 28–29 (printed pp. xxvi–xxvii) and contains tool screenshots, not additional statistical tables. The entire markdown was read through the references, acknowledgements and declaration on PDF pp. 40–41 (printed pp. xxxviii–xxxix).
This is an original experiment rather than a synthesis; synthesis study counts and pooled estimates are not applicable (PDF pp. 12–15, printed pp. 10–13, sections 4–5).
summary: The paper reports a randomized AI-assistance experiment with 70 students and belongs in the two-screener pipeline. Both recorded results and the one-line finding match the PDF, but the form omits scored outcomes, the output count, and required outcome coding.
